top_choice_rationale: P002 rests on a specific, tested idea (Katori's magic-wavelength lattice cancelling the light shift so many atoms are interrogated at once) and a decisive demonstration (Ye's strontium clocks at the 10^-18 level), confirmed by independent laboratories, species and clock-to-clock comparisons. The credit splits cleanly into concept and demonstration within two names, and the citation can be scoped to the many-atom lattice so it stays distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes. I rank P001 second because the science is strong but the pairing mechanism, phase diagram and disorder effects are still unsettled, and the credit has open edges (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto; Cao and others). P003 is mature but its credit is the weakest, with four candidates for three places and Jaksch outside the list. Any of these is preferred to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no documented tie to the lattice-clock, twisted-graphene or ultracold-atom candidates (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGO+ and XL-Calibur collaborations are unrelated)
